title: Mean, Median and Mode (Measures of Central Tendency)
seo_title: Mean, Median and Mode – Primary 5 Mathematics Worksheets with Answers (NERDC)
standard_text: Find the mean, median and mode of a set of data; find the range; solve problems on averages. (summary of the NERDC Primary 5 Mathematics curriculum)
meta_desc: Free Primary 5 maths worksheets on averages: the mean, the median, the mode and the range of a set of data, with problems on test scores and missing numbers. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Median: the middle. Mode: the most common.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Mean: add all the values and divide by how many there are.
  • Median: arrange the values in order and take the middle one. If there are two middle values, find the number halfway between them.
  • Mode: the value that appears most often. Range: highest − lowest.

Examples

Example

4, 9, 6, 9, 7

Mean = 35 ÷ 5 = 7

In order 4, 6, 7, 9, 9

Answer: mean 7, median 7, mode 9

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Forgetting to order the values for the medianArrange them first.
Dividing by the wrong numberDivide by how many values there are.
Giving how often for the modeThe mode is the value itself.

Usman swam a length of the pool 4 times. His times were 20.3, 20.5, 20.6 and 16.6 seconds. What was his mean time?
items.e: Total: 20.3 + 20.5 + 20.6 + 16.6 = 78.0. There are 4 lengths, so divide by 4: 78.0 ÷ 4 = 19.5 s.

items.q: The highest temperatures in Brighton during one week in July were 27, 25, 21, 17, 19, 18 and 27 °C. What was the mean highest temperature?
items.e: Total: 27 + 25 + 21 + 17 + 19 + 18 + 27 = 154. There are 7 days, so divide by 7: 154 ÷ 7 = 22 °C.

items.q: In a reading challenge, 5 pupils in Primary 5 read a mean of 7 books each and 10 pupils in Primary 6 read a mean of 10 books each. What was the mean for all 15 pupils?
items.e: Totals: 5 × 7 = 35 and 10 × 10 = 100. All together: 135 books for 15 pupils. Mean: 135 ÷ 15 = 9. (Do not just find the mean of 7 and 10: the groups are different sizes.)

items.q: Bisi’s scores on 3 spelling tests (out of 20) were 18, 16 and 11. What does she need to score on the next one to have a mean of 14?
items.e: For a mean of 14 over 4 tests, the total must be 4 × 14 = 56. So far: 18 + 16 + 11 = 45. Bisi needs 56 − 45 = 11.

items.q: The school football team scored 0, 2, 4, 4, 1 and 4 goals in its last 6 matches. What was the mean number of goals per match?
items.e: Total: 0 + 2 + 4 + 4 + 1 + 4 = 15. There are 6 matches (count the 0 too), so divide by 6: 15 ÷ 6 = 2.5.

items.q: Peter’s mean score in 3 games was 16. Gbenga’s mean score in 4 games was 13. Who scored more points in total, and how many more?
items.e: Peter: 16 × 3 = 48 points. Gbenga: 13 × 4 = 52 points. Gbenga scored 52 − 48 = 4 more. A higher mean does not always mean a higher total.

items.q: The mean mass of 3 bags of flour is 1.2 kg. What is the total mass of the 3 bags?
items.e: Total = mean × number of bags = 1.2 × 3 = 3.6 kg.

items.q: In a quiz, the 4 Robins scored 19, 25, 17 and 23 points and the 6 Owls scored 17, 14, 22, 18, 9 and 16 points. How much greater is the Robins’ mean score than the Owls’?
items.e: Robins: 84 ÷ 4 = 21. Owls: 96 ÷ 6 = 16. Difference: 21 − 16 = 5. (The Owls have the greater total, but they have more players, so compare the means.)

items.q: In a quiz, the 4 Hawks scored 7, 10, 12 and 11 points and the 6 Falcons scored 7, 3, 9, 14, 4 and 5 points. How much greater is the Hawks’ mean score than the Falcons’?
items.e: Hawks: 40 ÷ 4 = 10. Falcons: 42 ÷ 6 = 7. Difference: 10 − 7 = 3. (The Falcons have the greater total, but they have more players, so compare the means.)

items.q: A school has 4 classes with a mean of 29 pupils per class. A new class of 19 pupils joins the school. What is the new mean number of pupils per class?
items.e: Pupils before: 4 × 29 = 116. Now: 116 + 19 = 135 pupils in 5 classes. New mean: 135 ÷ 5 = 27.
